# llms.txt — agent entry index for gogogo

> gogogo — agent-native product foundation in Go: one binary with DB, auth, jobs,
> realtime and offline sync, and a CLI/MCP the agent drives to build it. Not a framework.
>
> Read AGENTS.md first. It points here for orientation; this file points
> everywhere else. Fetch only what the task needs — do not read the whole
> tree "to be safe" (see `cali-code-navigation`: orient with ripwire first).

## Start here (every task)

- **Deciding to use gogogo at all, or adopting it** — skills/gogogo-adopt/SKILL.md: the ask-before-scaffolding rule (name, owner, directory, shape, languages are the operator's call), what this is NOT for (a static/landing/conversion page — `GET /` is a redirect to /login), MCP vs CLI, and the port path for an existing app. Read it before proposing a scaffold.
- AGENTS.md — commands, don'ts, architecture seams (20-30 lines, normative)
- docs/glossary.md — the ubiquitous language: ONE meaning per term (recipe, receipt, declaration, capability, kind, unit, slot, metric, outcome, panel, drift, catalog) and the words that were retired. A term not listed there has no agreed meaning yet; a new term is defined there in the same commit.
- ARCHITECTURE.md — module layout and seams
- skills/gogogo-coding-standards/SKILL.md — Go + template rules (read when editing .go; on a .templ edit also read the UI skill below for the Datastar/backend gate)
- skills/gogogo-ui/SKILL.md — template UI rules over the vendored DaisyUI vocabulary (read before any .templ/CSS edit, with docs/ui-themes.md)
- skills/gogogo-recipe-authoring/SKILL.md — extension authoring contract (read before creating a feature, installing/editing a recipe, filling a slot, or declaring routes/tables/jobs/metrics)
- Measuring a recipe (an outcome is the job as a success/total pair of counts, no event stream, propose-then-confirm): skills/gogogo-recipe-authoring/references/metrics.md. Find what a recipe already counts with `recipe describe <id>` (or MCP `recipe_describe`) — metrics (activity and outcome kinds) are in its JSON — and validate a declaration with `recipe check <id>` (CLI) or MCP `recipe_check`. Rationale, not procedure: docs/research/recipe-outcomes-2026-11.md
- Two surfaces, never conflated: `cmd/gogogo` + `cmd/gogogo-mcp` are the **evolution** tools (developer only, may rewrite a checkout); a product's users/agents use `cmd/web` routes + `POST /api/ext/invoke` under session/RBAC. `recipe invoke` / `recipe_invoke` are developer clients of that route, not a product MCP. Details: docs/mcp.md#installer-surface-vs-product-surface.
- Scope rails are the operator's, set by env before the client spawns the server: `GOGOGO_READONLY=1` (mutations refuse; advise/plan/check keep working) and `GOGOGO_ALLOWED_ROOTS` (confine `--dir`). Details: docs/mcp.md#safeties-what-the-operator-sets-not-the-model.

## By task

- New feature or product plan: docs/overview.md, docs/features.md
- **Scaffolding a product.** `gogogo --name X --owner Y --no-tui --yes` (agents always pin `--yes`; preview with `--dry-run --format json`). **Ask the operator first** — name, owner, target dir, shape and `locales --set …` are their decisions, and a wrong name becomes the module path and the repository; `confirm:true` on MCP is a guard, not consent. Two flags decide what the tree ships: `--shape full|web|api|desktop|gui|mobile` prunes entrypoints (never changes what a page shows), and `--recipes none|all|<ids>` drops demo slices — `none` is the default and removal is gated on real imports, so a slice your tree still uses stays and the plan names the importer. Semantics: docs/shape.md (the closed enum, `.gogogo/shape.yml`, `make check-shape`, `APP_SHAPE` at runtime) and docs/cli.md. The new tree carries skills/ but does not re-register them in `.agents/skills/` — run `npx skills add <owner>/<repo>` or link each one by hand.
- Creating a feature or extension (recipe contract — what a recipe may own, what it must never touch, slots, metrics, update path): skills/gogogo-recipe-authoring/SKILL.md; reference slice: features/todo (in-tree); instrumented example: features/kiosk (bundled, declares an outcome metric)
- **Working without a checkout (the third-party path).** Nothing here requires cloning the template: `go install github.com/calionauta/gogogo/cmd/gogogo@latest` (or `.../cmd/gogogo-mcp@latest`, or `curl install.sh`) gives the whole evolution surface. Then, in order: `advise --need "..."` → `recipe source <id>` (read a slice's code; no receipt, no copy) → write your own, or `recipe install <id>` only when the copy must be owned and updatable. `capabilities_list` / `advise_stack` / `recipe_describe` answer "what exists" over MCP without any tree. Do NOT copy the template to read a pattern.
- **Languages the product ships**: `gogogo locales` (reads `locales.yml`, names the source), `gogogo locales --set en,pt-BR,es` (records it once). Everything downstream — `new feature` catalogs, `recipe check`, `make check-locales` — grades against that answer, so ask it before scaffolding a slice in a second language.
- Adding a dependency, or writing something a library could do (write-vs-rent,
  the ordered procedure, the four human-gated cases): docs/dependency-principles.md
- Search layers (substring / fuzzy / BM25), the runtime picker, how the layer degrades when removed: docs/search.md
- What a unit owns (routes, generated queries, removal path): docs/unit-contracts.md
  (generated; scaffold with `gogogo new feature <name>`)
- Editing a feature slice (its written boundary — owns / does not own / language / invariants, gated by `make check-domains`): docs/domain-cards.md and docs/domain/<id>.md
- Languages (what the product ships; one tracked record read by the boot, `new feature` and `recipe check`; `gogogo locales --set en,pt-BR`; metric labels translated in the declaration's `translations:` block; gate `make check-locales`): docs/configuration.md (SUPPORTED_LOCALES / DEFAULT_LOCALE) and skills/gogogo-recipe-authoring/SKILL.md § Strings
- Choosing a shape, or explaining why a target is absent (closed enum, one record, gate): docs/shape.md
- Removing a unit, or deciding what is safe to delete (removal class core/servant/feature — the registry's `Kind`; features via `recipe uninstall`, servants by hand, core never): docs/scope-taxonomy.md
- Architecture details: docs/architecture.md, docs/architecture-decision.md
- Config and env vars: docs/configuration.md
- Local CI and gates: docs/local-ci.md
- Keeping a scaffolded project current (base marker, --check-update, migrate, `migrate --files` for which files apply to you, `advise --intent update`; installed recipes: `recipe outdated` against the reviewed catalog): docs/upgrading.md
- Taking one unit into an app that already exists (read-only export bundle + porting checklist): docs/porting-into-an-existing-app.md
- Realtime, queue, offline: docs/async-layers.md; the transport decision tree (no poll, one stream per page, leader tab + BroadcastChannel): docs/realtime-recipe.md#global-state-and-the-connection-budget
- Hooks, outbound webhooks and analytics (one event bus, sinks, the UI beacon attribute, what is deliberately not built): docs/hooks-analytics.md
- Auth and sessions: internal/auth/ (owned argon2id sessions), features/authviews/ (login UI)
- Security model, audit trail, CSP reporting, secrets/email, production defaults: docs/security.md
  (details: docs/rbac.md, docs/admin-dashboard.md, docs/deploy.md, docs/architecture.md#security-boundary)
- AI credits and billing: docs/llm-and-credits.md, features/credits/
- Installer (scaffold / new feature / recipes): internal/installer/, cmd/gogogo/README.md
  (`gogogo new feature <name>` scaffolds one unit; MCP equivalent: `new_feature`). After editing a file a recipe owns, `gogogo recipe receipts --write` re-hashes it — the `receipt-hashes` hook and `make check-recipes` fail until you do.
- Preflight/codegen (read-only checks, deterministic generate): `gogogo doctor --json` + `gogogo generate --check` — see docs/doctor-generate.md, skill ref references/doctor-generate.md
- Desktop strategy (PWA-only vs Wails / gogpu/ui / MyGo — confirm with operator before changing shell): docs/desktop-mobile.md § Choosing a desktop strategy, § Desktop authentication strategy (own gogogo_auth loopback vs federated OAuth RFC 8252 system browser); MyGo shell proof + build recipe: docs/research/mygo-2026-11.md (`make mygo`, `cmd/mygo`)
- Going without auth/database (fork recipe): docs/no-auth-no-db-recipe.md
- HTTP route inventory (generated, do not edit): docs/api-routes.md
- UI work (MUST read before any .templ/CSS edit): skills/gogogo-ui/SKILL.md — template UI rules (DaisyUI vocabulary, semantic colors, compiled app.min.css) over the vendored skills/daisyui/SKILL.md vocabulary (byte-identical to https://daisyui.com/SKILL.md); guide in docs/ui-themes.md, theme catalog in internal/themes
- Adding a native panel to Chat (`todo_list`-style): reuse the feature's own page components, never a copy — contract in features/genui/components/panel.go, reference in features/todo/handlers/genui_panel.go + features/todo/components/panel.templ; guide: docs/native-panels.md
- Deploy: docs/deploy.md
- Troubleshooting: docs/troubleshooting.md

## Every published page

Generated from site/docsite.config.mjs by `make docs-index`; the guard fails on drift.
`docs/<file>` is the source, the URL is where it renders, and `docs/<file>.md`-style
markdown copies are published beside each page for an agent that wants one page
without the whole site.

**Get started**
- [overview](https://calionauta.github.io/gogogo/docs/overview/) — What gogogo is, who it is for, why its gates exist, and the seven async layers it ships. (`docs/overview.md`)
- [motivation](https://calionauta.github.io/gogogo/docs/motivation/) — The thesis behind the stack: Go for almost everything, Zig as the named exception, and how to choose without hype. (`docs/motivation.md`)
- [architecture-decision](https://calionauta.github.io/gogogo/docs/architecture-decision/) — The flat-stack decision record: what it serves, what it replaced, and the migration it completed. (`docs/architecture-decision.md`)
- [inspirations](https://calionauta.github.io/gogogo/docs/inspirations/) — What gogogo learned from other projects, credited rather than vendored. (`docs/inspirations.md`)
- [getting-started](https://calionauta.github.io/gogogo/docs/getting-started/) — Clone, run, first five minutes, and the commands you need. (`docs/getting-started.md`)
- [glossary](https://calionauta.github.io/gogogo/docs/glossary/) — The ubiquitous language: one meaning per term (recipe, receipt, declaration, capability, kind, slot, metric, outcome, panel, drift) and the words that were retired. (`docs/glossary.md`)


**Agents**
- [cli](https://calionauta.github.io/gogogo/docs/cli/) — The evolution CLI: scaffold, doctor/generate, recipe, export, new feature, migrate. Developer surface; product clients use the server API. (`docs/cli.md`)
- [mcp](https://calionauta.github.io/gogogo/docs/mcp/) — The evolution MCP over stdio, its tools, and the split from the product surface (POST /api/ext/invoke). Installer only; never ship it to end users. (`docs/mcp.md`)
- [prompts](https://calionauta.github.io/gogogo/docs/prompts/) — Model-facing text lives in .prompt files (Dotprompt shape): layout, the check-prompts gate, instrumentation by id/version, and the GEPA workflow. (`docs/prompts.md`)

- [rbac](https://calionauta.github.io/gogogo/docs/rbac/) — Casbin RBAC: role vocabulary, the feature checklist, hint-vs-enforcement, and the two invariants that bite (authentication is not authorization; policy objects are paths, not regex). (`docs/rbac.md`)

- [exception-to-go](https://calionauta.github.io/gogogo/docs/exception-to-go/) — Go-first policy: why Zig is an exceptional native boundary, the agent decision procedure, and the isolation, testing, and removal rules. (`docs/exception-to-go.md`)
- [native-language-tradeoffs](https://calionauta.github.io/gogogo/docs/native-language-tradeoffs/) — Evidence-backed tradeoffs of Zig, Rust, Nim, Odin, and Mojo as native exception languages, and what a non-Zig proposal must rebut. (`docs/native-language-tradeoffs.md`)

(`docs/research/genui-schema-patterns-2026-11.md`)

- [supply-chain-scanning](https://calionauta.github.io/gogogo/docs/supply-chain-scanning/) — The 2026-10-24 SBOM/image-scanning comparison: Syft+Grype against Trivy, Docker Scout and OSV-Scanner, with the pinned-action and fixable-high gate. (`docs/research/supply-chain-scanning-2026.md`)
- [native-kernels](https://calionauta.github.io/gogogo/docs/native-kernels/) — The 2026-10-25 native-kernel PoCs: FNV-1a tie vs grayscale survivor, SIMD verbs audit, loader prices, Rust/Odin probes. (`docs/research/native-kernels-2026-10.md`)
- [browser-automation](https://calionauta.github.io/gogogo/docs/browser-automation/) — chrome-headless-shell vs Lightpanda vs happy-dom vs remote CDP on a shared 8 GB box, and why a Playwright suite's lifecycle, not its engine, is what took the host down. (`docs/research/browser-automation-2026-10.md`)
- [notify](https://calionauta.github.io/gogogo/docs/notify/) — The 2026-10-27 notify evaluation: what to copy from a delivery engine, why the inbox stays local, and where an external provider fits. (`docs/research/notify-2026-10.md`)
- [ci-wall-clock](https://calionauta.github.io/gogogo/docs/ci-wall-clock/) — Where CI's minutes go, measured per job and per package: sharding by cost, PR-only test selection, narrow caches, and the options that were rejected with evidence. (`docs/research/ci-wall-clock-2026-10.md`)
- [ci-playbook-boardy](https://calionauta.github.io/gogogo/docs/ci-playbook-boardy/) — Owen Gretzinger's nine CI levers cross-checked against this repo: eight already shipped, the paid runner rejected, and the live gap — an untested docs-only skip classifier that can report green while skipping every heavy gate. (`docs/research/ci-playbook-boardy-2026-10.md`)
- [ci-provider-move](https://calionauta.github.io/gogogo/docs/ci-provider-move/) — CircleCI, Dagger, Woodpecker and self-hosted evaluated against measured numbers: minutes are free on a public repo, the runner queue is 12s, and more cores cannot beat a 42s package tail — a provider move is cost without wall-clock. (`docs/research/ci-provider-move-2026-10.md`)
- [mobile-android](https://calionauta.github.io/gogogo/docs/mobile-android/) — The 2026-10-30 Android spike: tursogo has no Android library, ncruces keeps SQL and migrations shared, cmd/gui chose ncruces explicitly, and cmd/mobile is the separate entrypoint. (`docs/research/mobile-android-2026-10.md`)
- [android-spike](https://calionauta.github.io/gogogo/docs/android-spike/) — The Android spike build log: commands, driver matrix, libc shims, system-bar insets, screenshots, disk usage and cleanup. (`docs/research/android-spike-2026-10.md`)
- [app-shapes](https://calionauta.github.io/gogogo/docs/app-shapes/) — One template, six products: a closed shape enum (web/api/desktop/gui/mobile/full) applied through the existing removal mechanics, recorded in .gogogo/shape.yml and proved by shape check. (`docs/research/app-shapes-2026-11.md`)
- [domain-first](https://calionauta.github.io/gogogo/docs/domain-first/) — What DDD buys an AI contributor: one domain card per bounded context (language, boundary, invariants), generated by the scaffolder and gated by check-domains, instead of aggregates and repository ceremony. (`docs/research/domain-first-2026-11.md`)
- [scaffold-choice](https://calionauta.github.io/gogogo/docs/scaffold-choice/) — Why the scaffold prompt offers only the installer units, the three lists that disagree, and the Scaffold class that makes every capability an explicit keep-or-drop. (`docs/research/scaffold-choice-2026-10.md`)
- [extensibility](https://calionauta.github.io/gogogo/docs/extensibility/) — Core plus installable extensions evaluated for 2026: why buildmode=plugin is out, why anchor-patching cannot carry N authors, what compile-time registration costs, and the ordered spikes that can kill the idea. (`docs/research/extensibility-2026-11.md`)
- [recipe-metrics-panel](https://calionauta.github.io/gogogo/docs/recipe-metrics-panel/) — Declarative dashboard metrics (one COUNT per entry) and chat panel spec: what was adopted vs. rejected, the SlicePanel base, the recipe-check evaluator, and the in-repo catalog decision. (`docs/research/recipe-metrics-panel-2026-11.md`)
- [recipe-outcomes](https://calionauta.github.io/gogogo/docs/recipe-outcomes/) — An outcome as two declared counts (success over eligible) instead of an event stream: the validation rules, the runtime warning, the dashboard ratio, why not a Taguchi S/N, and the propose/confirm authorship rule. (`docs/research/recipe-outcomes-2026-11.md`)
- [mygo](https://calionauta.github.io/gogogo/docs/mygo/) — MyGo peer shell over the flat stack: webview cookie + SSE proof, loopback vs native view, driver matrix, and the cmd/mygo build recipe. (`docs/research/mygo-2026-11.md`)
- [headless-cms-go](https://calionauta.github.io/gogogo/docs/headless-cms-go/) — The Go headless CMS ecosystem probed against the two-month window: why ocms-go and ridu are not adopted, the four GitHub-as-CMS models and what 'issues as pages' actually means, and why the content surface belongs in a recipe. (`docs/research/headless-cms-go-2026-11.md`)
- [i18n](https://calionauta.github.io/gogogo/docs/i18n/) — UI internationalization: own the seam on the text package, rent CLDR depth only on a trigger. The libraries evaluated, mitigations for their gaps, and the phased, deletable plan. (`docs/research/i18n-2026-11.md`)


**Ship**
- [deploy](https://calionauta.github.io/gogogo/docs/deploy/) — Server layout, first-time setup, deploy workflow, build pipeline and version badge. (`docs/deploy.md`)

- [admin-dashboard](https://calionauta.github.io/gogogo/docs/admin-dashboard/) — Admin surfaces, the single-cookie session, and the DagNats console. (`docs/admin-dashboard.md`)


**Operate**
- [upgrading](https://calionauta.github.io/gogogo/docs/upgrading/) — Keeping a scaffolded project current: the recorded base revision, --check-update's two halves, and migrate as a list plus gates — never a merge. (`docs/upgrading.md`)
- [local-ci](https://calionauta.github.io/gogogo/docs/local-ci/) — The five-tier feedback loop and make signoff. (`docs/local-ci.md`)
- [ci-triage](https://calionauta.github.io/gogogo/docs/ci-triage/) — When CI fails on something variable: the 60-second triage, flake diagnosis, quarantine with an expiry, and why 100% is not the target. (`docs/ci-triage.md`)
- [code-quality](https://calionauta.github.io/gogogo/docs/code-quality/) — The linter set, how to scope it, the Datastar-specific rules, and the ruleguard rules that encode project footguns as CI failures. (`docs/code-quality.md`)
- [troubleshooting](https://calionauta.github.io/gogogo/docs/troubleshooting/) — Symptoms and where they actually come from. (`docs/troubleshooting.md`)
- [duckdb](https://calionauta.github.io/gogogo/docs/duckdb/) — Query JSONL logs and the Turso file with DuckDB: local operator recipe. (`docs/duckdb.md`)
- [doctor-generate](https://calionauta.github.io/gogogo/docs/doctor-generate/) — Doctor (read-only preflight, JSON for agents) and deterministic generate (templ+sqlc+css+docs) — the LLM-era determinism layer. (`docs/doctor-generate.md`)
<!-- page-index:end -->

## Invariants (do not relearn these)

- Concurrency: `-race` proves no unsafe memory access, NOT that an interleaving
  is correct. A decision and the action it licenses are ONE lock hold — releasing
  between "where does this go" and "put it there" loses the update silently, and
  channels make it race-free. Errors inside their own nil-check never get here
  (ruleguard `SwallowedErrorInCheck`); temporal properties (`a call must not
  outlive its lease`) need a model, not a linter. Details and the three failure
  modes:
  `skills/gogogo-coding-standards/references/go-concurrency-deltas.md#lost-updates-the-bugs--race-cannot-see`.

- Flat stack only: chi handlers + dbgen queries, no framework.
- A new direct dependency needs a pass through docs/dependency-principles.md and
  a one-line trade-off record in the PR body; raising the native floor (a new
  CGO/native library, build tool, or runtime library) is a human gate.
- `go run ./cmd/check-flatdeps` proves it — run before committing.
- Not a framework, and it is enforced: `go run ./cmd/check-product-boundary` fails
  when `cmd/web` imports the evolution tools (`internal/installer`,
  `internal/capabilities`, `internal/shape`, `cmd/gogogo*`) or when the installer
  imports the server. The product binary must build after they are deleted.
- Generated code is committed and drift-checked (`make check-generated`).
- Counts are generated, never hand-written: `docs/unit-contracts.md` is the source; `make check-docs` gates counts, dead paths, invented subcommands, and MANIFEST coverage.
- `//nolint` is last resort (skill documents the procedure; CI enforces it).
- Security events are durable (`security_events`, 30-day batched retention); request-scoped
  logs go through `internal/observability`, never bare `slog` in a handler.
- Global/shell state reuses a stream; never poll. One long-lived connection per
  page (six-per-host budget; five same-user tabs fill it). Pages without a
  feature stream use `session.js` (leader + BroadcastChannel);
  `TestNoPeriodicFetch` rejects `data-on-interval` fetches. Recipe:
  docs/realtime-recipe.md#global-state-and-the-connection-budget.
- Never edit `site/docs/` (generated output).
